title: The Lekki Headmaster
author: Kabir Alabi Garba
synopsis: The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba is a poignant, high-yield prose narrative prescribed for the JAMB UTME Use of English examination. Set in the high-brow maritime corridor of Lekki, Lagos State, at the prestigious Stardom Schools, the novel chronicles the professional, philosophical, and psychological trials of Mr. Adebepo Adewale (popularly known as "Bepo" or "The Lekki Headmaster"). A passionate educator of exceptional probity, Bepo finds himself trapped between unwavering devotion to mentoring Nigeria's future generation and the relentless societal and familial pressure to relocate abroad ("Japa"). Through emotional breakdowns, staff camaraderie, institutional power struggles, and profound introspective awakening, the text interrogates the socio-economic fault lines of contemporary Nigeria.

chapters.title: Dusk: The Morning Assembly Breakdown
chapters.summary:
At the morning assembly, Principal Bepo Adewale suddenly cannot talk.   

He walks to the podium looking sad and starts to cry in front of everyone.   

The Vice Principal (Mrs. Grace Apeh) and other staff try to find out what is wrong, but Bepo does not say anything.   

He is taken to his office, still weeping.   News of his strange behaviour reaches some parents and the Managing Director (MD), Mrs. Ibidun Gloss, is called to the school.   

She questions Bepo, but he only keeps saying, "I will be all right."   Even a pastor-teacher (Mr. Ope Wonde) is invited to talk to him too, but Bepo still will not explain his problem.   

The MD later learns that Bepo's wife now lives in London.   In the end, Bepo is asked to go home to rest.

chapters.title: The Enticement
chapters.summary:
We learn why Bepo was crying: he has decided to relocate (japa) to the United Kingdom.   

His wife (Seri) and their two children (Nike and Kike) are already in the UK, and Seri has been pressuring him to join them.   

But Bepo loves his job and his students at Stardom Schools, where he has worked for over 20 years and earned the nickname "The Lekki Headmaster".  

 His colleagues think he is foolish to be sad about such a "golden opportunity".   

People compare his Nigerian salary to what he could earn in pounds in the UK.   But Bepo had wanted to start his own transport or private school business when he retired.

chapters.title: Migration Tales
chapters.summary:
Bepo starts researching what life is like for Nigerians who have moved abroad.   

He learns about hourly wages in the UK, USA and Canada, and how much people can earn compared to Nigeria.   

He hears stories of Nigerians selling everything to relocate.   Some borrowing money and never paying back.   And even people who stole to fund their travel.   

His former colleague (Sola) who now lives in the UK, tells him about her experience — the good side like free healthcare and schools, and the opposite like low-paying jobs and expensive rent.   

Not every migration story is a success; some people abroad struggle badly

chapters.title: A Case of Visa Denied
chapters.summary:
A parent (Mrs. Ignatius) calls Bepo late at night to complain that her husband (Ibe) has not come home.   

Their family had planned to relocate to London, but their visa was denied because a DNA test showed that Mr. Ignatius is not the biological father of one of their three children.   

This discovery has caused serious trouble in the marriage, and Ibe threatens to leave his wife and the child who is not his.   

This chapter shows another side of the japa dream — how family secrets can be exposed by the visa process and how emigration is not always simple or happy.

chapters.title: Snake in the Roof
chapters.summary:
During lunch break, the MD (Mrs. Ibidun Gloss), goes to inspect a piece of land that the school owns.   

She is shocked to find many staff cars and big vehicles parked there secretly.   

She fears that teachers are stealing school money to buy these cars.   

She calls the accountant and principal to explain.   It turns out the money came from the school's staff cooperative society, which had grown very large — #95 million in the account, with #50 million loaned out.   

Worried that the cooperative has become too powerful (like "a snake in the roof"), the board of directors decides to limit how much any staff member can borrow, to protect the school from future risk.

quiz.question: What contrast does Bepo draw between historic slavery and modern migration in Chapter 9?

quiz.question: How does Chapter 9 foreshadow the climax of the novel in Chapters 11 and 12?

quiz.question: What mood surrounds Bepo's reflections during the Badagry excursion?

quiz.question: What does the phrase "Point of No Return" symbolize in Chapter 9?

quiz.optionB: The irreversible separation of Africans from their homeland, paralleled with permanent emigration

quiz.question: What role does Stardom Schools' excursion culture play in Bepo's reputation as a headmaster?

chapters.title: Passport Pains
chapters.summary:
Bepo faces frustrating problems trying to renew his expired Nigerian passport.   

Because of large crowds and long delays at the Lagos passport office, he decides to travel to Ibadan for a faster process.   

On the journey, Bepo reflects on the changes he sees along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway — new roads, businesses and religious buildings.   

He ends up paying extra money to an agent (Tai) to speed things up, which shows how common bribery and "connection" are in government processes.   

Even after paying the agent, Bepo still faces more delays at the National Identity Number (NIN) office, which puts his travel date at risk

quiz.question: What is the title of Chapter 10 in The Lekki Headmaster?
quiz.optionA: Point of No Return
quiz.optionB: Passport Pains
quiz.optionC: A Case of Visa Denied
quiz.optionD: ...Dawn
quiz.explanation: Chapter 10 is titled "Passport Pains," chronicling the bureaucratic hurdles Bepo faces while renewing his expired Nigerian passport[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Why does Principal Bepo decide to travel from Lagos to Ibadan in Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: To attend a national conference of private school principals
quiz.optionB: To avoid massive crowds and long delays at the Lagos passport office
quiz.optionC: To visit his wife Seri's family home
quiz.optionD: To inspect a branch of Stardom Schools in Oyo State
quiz.explanation: Frustrated by heavy congestion and slow processing at the Lagos passport office, Bepo heads to Ibadan hoping for a faster renewal[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What does Bepo observe along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway during his journey to Ibadan?
quiz.optionA: Abandoned farmland and flooded villages
quiz.optionB: Rapid physical development including new roads, businesses, and religious buildings
quiz.optionC: Military checkpoints every two kilometers
quiz.optionD: Street protests by university students
quiz.explanation: Along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, Bepo reflects on the visible growth of new roads, commercial enterprises, and religious centers[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Who is Tai in Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: Bepo's younger brother who works at the airport
quiz.optionB: An agent whom Bepo pays extra money to speed up his passport renewal
quiz.optionC: The immigration comptroller in Ibadan
quiz.optionD: A senior prefect at Stardom Schools
quiz.explanation: Bepo ends up paying extra money to an agent named Tai to expedite his passport renewal process[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What systemic problem in Nigerian public administration does Bepo's interaction with Tai expose?
quiz.optionA: Lack of computer literacy among bank tellers
quiz.optionB: How widespread bribery and informal "connection" networks have become in official government processes
quiz.optionC: The refusal of immigration offices to accept Naira payments
quiz.optionD: Overstaffing at federal ministries
quiz.explanation: Paying an agent extra money to bypass bottlenecks highlights how entrenched bribery and "connection" are in public service delivery[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Which additional government agency causes further delays for Bepo even after he pays the agent?
quiz.optionA: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
quiz.optionB: The National Identity Number (NIN) office
quiz.optionC: The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)
quiz.optionD: The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB)
quiz.explanation: Even after paying Tai, Bepo encounters frustrating delays at the National Identity Number (NIN) office[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What serious consequence do the delays at the passport and NIN offices create for Bepo?
quiz.optionA: His UK visa is permanently revoked
quiz.optionB: His planned travel date is put at risk
quiz.optionC: He loses his job at Stardom Schools before his farewell
quiz.optionD: He is arrested for double registration
quiz.explanation: The compounded bottlenecks at both the passport and NIN offices threaten to make him miss his scheduled departure date[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What internal conflict does Bepo's reliance on an agent (Tai) represent?
quiz.optionA: A principled man forced to navigate a corrupt, inefficient bureaucracy just to get basic documentation
quiz.optionB: A corrupt principal looking for ways to defraud the government
quiz.optionC: An opportunist trying to start an immigration agency in Ibadan
quiz.optionD: A teacher who refuses to follow any official guidelines
quiz.explanation: Even a man of high integrity like Bepo finds himself trapped by a broken system where paying extra to middlemen is treated as the only way forward[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Why was Bepo renewing his Nigerian passport in Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: Because his previous passport had expired before his planned trip to the UK
quiz.optionB: Because he lost his passport during the Badagry excursion
quiz.optionC: Because his wife Seri tore his old passport
quiz.optionD: Because he wanted to apply for a Canadian diplomatic visa
quiz.explanation: Bepo needed to renew his expired Nigerian passport so he could travel to join his family in the United Kingdom[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What does Bepo's reflection on the new buildings and businesses along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway reveal?
quiz.optionA: That Nigeria has zero economic activity outside Lekki
quiz.optionB: His observant nature and appreciation of the energy, growth, and potential within Nigeria
quiz.optionC: His desire to become a real estate developer in Ogun State
quiz.optionD: His anger over traffic congestion caused by churches
quiz.explanation: As he travels, Bepo notices signs of enterprise and development along the corridor, reflecting his deep connection to his homeland[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Which two cities are central to Bepo's passport renewal journey in Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: Lagos and Abuja
quiz.optionB: Lagos and Ibadan
quiz.optionC: Ibadan and Abeokuta
quiz.optionD: Lekki and Badagry
quiz.explanation: Unable to endure the delays in Lagos, Bepo travels to Ibadan to process his passport renewal[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How does Chapter 10 contribute to the novel's portrayal of the "japa" experience?
quiz.optionA: It shows that preparing to leave Nigeria involves exhausting bureaucratic stress and extra financial costs
quiz.optionB: It proves that Nigerian government offices operate with instant efficiency
quiz.optionC: It suggests that only residents of Ibadan can obtain passports
quiz.optionD: It shows that NIN is not required for international travel
quiz.explanation: The chapter illustrates the frustrating administrative hurdles—crowds, middlemen, and NIN delays—that emigrants must endure before leaving[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What ironic situation does Bepo face in Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: He travels to Ibadan for speed, pays an agent to hasten things, yet still gets stalled at the NIN office
quiz.optionB: He forgets to bring any passport photographs to Ibadan
quiz.optionC: He arrives at the passport office on a public holiday
quiz.optionD: He accidentally renews his driver's license instead of his passport
quiz.explanation: Despite leaving Lagos for a faster process and paying Tai extra, Bepo is still held up by NIN verification delays[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Which documentation hurdle almost derails Bepo's departure schedule in Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: Missing primary school certificate
quiz.optionB: Expired Nigerian passport and National Identity Number (NIN) processing delays
quiz.optionC: Unpaid tenement rates in Lekki
quiz.optionD: Expired yellow fever vaccination card
quiz.explanation: Both the passport renewal and NIN office delays put Bepo's scheduled flight at serious risk[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What tone characterizes Chapter 10?
quiz.optionA: Lighthearted comedy from start to finish
quiz.optionB: Satirical frustration over bureaucratic inefficiency and institutional bottlenecks
quiz.optionC: Gothic horror and suspense
quiz.optionD: Romantic nostalgia
quiz.explanation: Through Bepo's ordeal with crowds, middlemen, and NIN delays, the chapter satirizes the exhausting inefficiencies of public institutions[cite: 6].

chapters.title: Point of No Return
chapters.summary:
The school organizes a big farewell party for Bepo.   

There are games, a debate, comedy skits mimicking Bepo's habits and traditional Nigerian dances, including a Canoe dance from Badagry.   

During the dance, Bepo becomes so emotional (remembering the slave history again) that he shouts out loud, disturbing the performance — but he quickly calms the crowd with a joke.   

The MD gives a moving speech praising Bepo's 24 years of service and presents him with a cheque of $10,000 as a farewell gift.   

Bepo is overcome with emotion and cries as he tries to give his thank-you speech.

quiz.question: What is the title of Chapter 11 in The Lekki Headmaster?
quiz.optionA: Dusk...
quiz.optionB: Point of No Return
quiz.optionC: ...Dawn
quiz.optionD: Missions Unaccomplished
quiz.explanation: Chapter 11 is titled "Point of No Return," capturing the emotional farewell event organized for Bepo at Stardom Schools[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What major event does Stardom Schools organize for Bepo in Chapter 11?
quiz.optionA: A surprise birthday party
quiz.optionB: A grand farewell party
quiz.optionC: An inter-house sports festival
quiz.optionD: A fundraising gala for the Invention Club
quiz.explanation: The school community hosts an elaborate farewell party to celebrate Bepo's years of leadership before his departure[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Which activities feature during Bepo's farewell party in Chapter 11?
quiz.optionA: Swimming competitions and chess tournaments
quiz.optionB: Games, a debate, comedy skits mimicking Bepo's habits, and traditional Nigerian dances
quiz.optionC: Science exhibitions and spelling bees
quiz.optionD: Poetry recitals by parents only
quiz.explanation: The farewell celebration includes games, a debate, humorous skits imitating Bepo's mannerisms, and traditional dances[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Which specific traditional dance performed at the farewell party triggers a strong emotional reaction from Bepo?
quiz.optionA: The Bata dance from Oyo
quiz.optionB: The Canoe dance from Badagry
quiz.optionC: The Atilogwu dance from Anambra
quiz.optionD: The Swange dance from Benue
quiz.explanation: The performance of the Canoe dance from Badagry stirs deep emotions in Bepo[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Why does Bepo shout out loud and disturb the Canoe dance performance during his farewell party?
quiz.optionA: Because a dancer fell off the stage
quiz.optionB: Because the Badagry dance reminds him once again of the painful history of the slave trade and his own departure
quiz.optionC: Because the sound system broke down
quiz.optionD: Because he was angry at the students mimicking his habits
quiz.explanation: Watching the Badagry Canoe dance triggers memories of the slave trade and the "Point of No Return," causing him to cry out involuntarily[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How does Bepo quickly recover the mood of the audience after shouting out during the dance?
quiz.optionA: He walks out of the hall in silence
quiz.optionB: He quickly calms the crowd with a joke
quiz.optionC: He asks the Managing Director to stop the music
quiz.optionD: He delivers a stern lecture on history
quiz.explanation: Showing his trademark wit and composure, Bepo immediately cracks a joke to ease the tension and reassure everyone[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How many years of service does the Managing Director praise Bepo for in her farewell speech?
quiz.optionA: 15 years
quiz.optionB: 20 years
quiz.optionC: 24 years
quiz.optionD: 30 years
quiz.explanation: In her moving tribute, Mrs. Ibidun Gloss commends Bepo for 24 years of dedicated service to Stardom Schools[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What farewell gift does the Managing Director present to Bepo on behalf of the school?
quiz.optionA: A brand-new SUV
quiz.optionB: A cheque of $10,000
quiz.optionC: A plot of land in Lekki
quiz.optionD: A gold wristwatch and plaque
quiz.explanation: Mrs. Gloss presents Bepo with a generous farewell cheque of $10,000 in appreciation of his 24 years of service[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How does Bepo react when he steps forward to deliver his thank-you speech?
quiz.optionA: He criticizes the board for limiting the cooperative society
quiz.optionB: He is overcome with emotion and cries as he tries to speak
quiz.optionC: He announces that he has already canceled his flight
quiz.optionD: He hands the $10,000 cheque back to the MD
quiz.explanation: Deeply moved by the school's love, tribute, and $10,000 gift, Bepo breaks into tears while attempting his thank-you speech[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What do the comedy skits mimicking Bepo's habits reveal about how students view him?
quiz.optionA: They mock him out of hatred and disrespect
quiz.optionB: They observe him fondly and affectionately as a beloved, memorable mentor
quiz.optionC: They have never interacted with him closely
quiz.optionD: They want him to leave the school as soon as possible
quiz.explanation: Mimicking a leader's familiar mannerisms at a farewell party reflects warmth, affection, and close daily connection[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Why is Chapter 11 titled "Point of No Return"?
quiz.optionA: Because Bepo boards his flight to London in this chapter
quiz.optionB: Because the farewell party marks the emotional threshold of leaving his 24-year career, echoed by the Badagry slave-trade motif
quiz.optionC: Because the school gates are permanently locked after the party
quiz.optionD: Because the Managing Director refuses to ever rehire him
quiz.explanation: The title links Bepo's emotional farewell ceremony with the Badagry slave-trade symbol that resurfaces during the Canoe dance[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What does the $10,000 farewell gift signify about Bepo's impact on Stardom Schools?
quiz.optionA: That the school wanted to bribe him to keep quiet about the cooperative
quiz.optionB: That management and proprietors deeply valued his 24 years of transformational leadership
quiz.optionC: That Bepo had been underpaid for two decades
quiz.optionD: That foreign currency was the only money in the school account
quiz.explanation: Presenting a $10,000 cheque alongside a glowing speech demonstrates immense institutional gratitude for Bepo's loyalty and impact[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How does Bepo's reaction in Chapter 11 echo his breakdown in Chapter 1?
quiz.optionA: In both chapters, overwhelming emotion over leaving Stardom Schools brings him to tears in front of the school community
quiz.optionB: In both chapters, he refuses to speak a single word
quiz.optionC: In both chapters, he argues publicly with Mr. Guta
quiz.optionD: In both chapters, he collapses and is rushed to the hospital
quiz.explanation: Just as he wept on the assembly podium in Chapter 1, Bepo's deep love for the school moves him to tears during his farewell speech[cite: 3, 6].

quiz.question: Which combination of elements makes Chapter 11 both celebratory and poignant?
quiz.optionA: Lively games, debates, skits, and dances contrasted with Bepo's slave-history outburst and tearful farewell
quiz.optionB: A somber funeral procession followed by a staff strike
quiz.optionC: A courtroom trial followed by a graduation ceremony
quiz.optionD: An angry confrontation between parents and teachers
quiz.explanation: Joyous tributes, skits, and the $10,000 gift blend with Bepo's intense grief at parting from the school he loves[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What is the dominant atmosphere at the end of Chapter 11?
quiz.optionA: Bitter hostility
quiz.optionB: Deep gratitude, affection, and bittersweet emotion
quiz.optionC: Cold indifference
quiz.optionD: Comic relief without any sadness
quiz.explanation: The chapter closes on a deeply touching note of mutual love and sorrowful parting between Bepo and Stardom Schools[cite: 6].

chapters.title: Dawn: Return of the Master
chapters.summary:
Bepo prepares to travel to the UK, remembering an earlier time he missed a flight by misreading his ticket.   

This time, he is very careful.   His landlord's family comes to say goodbye, and his colleagues (the VP, accountant and other teachers) follow him to the airport.   

At the airport, Bepo checks in and later falls asleep while waiting to board.   

He has a frightening dream about the slave museum in Badagry, where he sees himself being forced onto a slave ship, and he wakes up screaming "Nooo!" just before the flight takes off.   

On the following Monday, students at Stardom Schools are sad that Bepo is gone — until, suddenly, he appears at the school gate!   

Bepo has decided not to leave Nigeria after all.   He tells everyone, "My heart is here!" and the students celebrate his return with joy.

quiz.question: What does Bepo's ultimate decision at the end of the novel suggest about national development?
quiz.optionA: Everyone should stay in Nigeria regardless of their circumstances
quiz.optionB: True fulfillment and nation-building require dedicated citizens who choose to invest their talents at home
quiz.optionC: Foreign education has no value for Nigerians
quiz.optionD: Private schools pay better than jobs in the United Kingdom
quiz.explanation: Bepo's return ("My heart is here!") underscores the theme of patriotism and finding purpose in building one's home country.

quiz.question: What is the title of the final chapter (Chapter 12) of The Lekki Headmaster?
quiz.optionA: Dusk...
quiz.optionB: ...Dawn
quiz.optionC: Homeward Bound
quiz.optionD: The New Beginning
quiz.explanation: Chapter 12 is titled "...Dawn," completing the day-cycle symmetry begun in Chapter 1 ("Dusk...")[cite: 3, 6].

quiz.question: What past travel mistake does Bepo recall as he prepares to go to the airport in Chapter 12?
quiz.optionA: Losing his luggage in Abuja
quiz.optionB: Missing a flight earlier in life because he misread his ticket
quiz.optionC: Boarding the wrong plane to Ghana
quiz.optionD: Forgetting his passport at Stardom Schools
quiz.explanation: Remembering an earlier occasion when he missed a flight by misreading his ticket, Bepo takes extra care with his travel preparations[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Who comes to bid Bepo goodbye and accompany him to the airport in Chapter 12?
quiz.optionA: Only his travel agent Tai
quiz.optionB: His landlord's family, who say goodbye, and his colleagues (the VP, accountant, and other teachers), who follow him to the airport
quiz.optionC: The Managing Director and Mr. Guta alone
quiz.optionD: Nobody, because he leaves secretly at midnight
quiz.explanation: Bepo's landlord's family bids him farewell, while the Vice Principal, accountant, and fellow teachers escort him to the airport[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What does Bepo do at the airport after checking in for his flight?
quiz.optionA: He immediately calls Seri to cancel his ticket
quiz.optionB: He falls asleep while waiting to board
quiz.optionC: He meets Mr. Ignatius at the departure lounge
quiz.optionD: He gives an impromptu lecture to airport staff
quiz.explanation: After completing check-in procedures, Bepo dozes off in the waiting area before boarding[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What frightening nightmare does Bepo have while sleeping at the airport?
quiz.optionA: That Stardom Schools has burned to the ground
quiz.optionB: That he is back at the slave museum in Badagry, being forced onto a slave ship
quiz.optionC: That his plane crashes into the Atlantic Ocean
quiz.optionD: That he is arrested by immigration officers in London
quiz.explanation: Bepo dreams vividly of the Badagry slave museum and sees himself being forcibly driven onto a slave ship[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How does Bepo wake up from his nightmare at the airport?
quiz.optionA: Smiling quietly to himself
quiz.optionB: Screaming "Nooo!" just before the flight takes off
quiz.optionC: Asking a flight attendant for a glass of water
quiz.optionD: Calling Mrs. Ibidun Gloss on the phone
quiz.explanation: Terrified by the vision of being forced onto a slave ship, Bepo wakes up screaming "Nooo!" right before boarding/takeoff[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What unexpected event happens at Stardom Schools on the Monday following Bepo's supposed departure?
quiz.optionA: The Managing Director announces the permanent closure of the school
quiz.optionB: While students are mourning Bepo's absence, he suddenly appears at the school gate
quiz.optionC: Seri arrives from London to take over as principal
quiz.optionD: The Invention Club cancels its phone project
quiz.explanation: On Monday morning, as saddened students miss him, Bepo shockingly turns up at the Stardom Schools gate[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What final decision does Bepo make regarding his relocation to the United Kingdom?
quiz.optionA: He postpones his trip for two weeks
quiz.optionB: He decides not to leave Nigeria after all
quiz.optionC: He decides to relocate to Canada instead of the UK
quiz.optionD: He returns only to collect his $10,000 cheque
quiz.explanation: Following his airport epiphany, Bepo abandons the relocation plan and chooses to remain in Nigeria[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What famous declaration does Bepo make to everyone upon returning to Stardom Schools?
quiz.optionA: "Nigeria will never change!"
quiz.optionB: "My heart is here!"
quiz.optionC: "The journey has just begun!"
quiz.optionD: "I have come to claim my throne!"
quiz.explanation: Bepo announces to the rejoicing school community, "My heart is here!"[cite: 6]

quiz.question: How do the students at Stardom Schools react to Bepo's return on Monday?
quiz.optionA: They are confused and disappointed
quiz.optionB: They celebrate his return with immense joy
quiz.optionC: They ignore him and continue their assembly
quiz.optionD: They ask him why he wasted his flight ticket
quiz.explanation: Overjoyed to see their beloved headmaster back, the students erupt in celebration[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What psychological role does Bepo's airport dream play in the resolution of the novel?
quiz.optionA: It is a meaningless dream caused by airport noise
quiz.optionB: It acts as his subconscious awakening, confirming that leaving Nigeria feels like voluntary enslavement against his true calling
quiz.optionC: It convinces him that flying is medically unsafe
quiz.optionD: It reminds him that he left his luggage with his landlord
quiz.explanation: The nightmare fuses the Badagry slave-ship imagery with his reluctance to leave, crystalizing his realization that his true purpose is in Nigeria[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Why is the final chapter titled "...Dawn"?
quiz.optionA: Because Bepo's flight departed at 5:00 a.m.
quiz.optionB: Because Bepo's return marks a fresh beginning, clarity of purpose, and renewed hope for him and Stardom Schools
quiz.optionC: Because the school changed its morning assembly time
quiz.optionD: Because Bepo decided to open a morning-shift school
quiz.explanation: "...Dawn" symbolizes renewal, light after emotional darkness, and Bepo's joyful recommitment to his vocation at home[cite: 6].

quiz.question: What does the loyalty of the landlord's family, VP, accountant, and teachers in Chapter 12 demonstrate?
quiz.optionA: They wanted to make sure Bepo actually left the country
quiz.optionB: Bepo's warmth and integrity earned him genuine love both at home and in the workplace
quiz.optionC: They were hoping to share his $10,000 farewell gift
quiz.optionD: The Managing Director forced them to go to the airport
quiz.explanation: Having both his neighbors and colleagues turn out to see him off reflects the deep affection Bepo inspires everywhere he lives and works[cite: 6].

quiz.question: How does Bepo's resolution in Chapter 12 address the novel's central "japa" debate?
quiz.optionA: It argues that foreign countries do not exist
quiz.optionB: It affirms that while relocation entices many, personal fulfillment and patriotism can triumph over external pressure to leave
quiz.optionC: It proves that Seri will divorce him immediately
quiz.optionD: It shows that money is the only factor in career decisions
quiz.explanation: By choosing "My heart is here!" over life in the UK, Bepo embodies devotion to purpose, community, and homeland[cite: 6].

quiz.question: Which structural parallel ties Chapter 1 and Chapter 12 together?
quiz.optionA: Both chapters take place at the Ibadan passport office
quiz.optionB: Chapter 1 opens at "Dusk..." with Bepo weeping in despair, while Chapter 12 closes at "...Dawn" with Bepo returning in joy
quiz.optionC: Both chapters feature Mr. Guta complaining about grammar
quiz.optionD: Both chapters end with Bepo boarding an international flight
quiz.explanation: The "Dusk..." to "...Dawn" arc frames Bepo's emotional journey from sorrowful reluctant departure to joyful homecoming[cite: 3, 6].

characters.name: Mr. Adebepo Adewale ("Bepo")
characters.significance: The moral and narrative anchor of the novel. An erudite, compassionate, and uncompromising school administrator at Stardom Schools, Lekki. His internal tug-of-war between dedication to Nigerian youth and intense family pressure to emigrate (Japa) forms the core conflict. His refusal to board at MMIA epitomizes moral courage and patriotism.

characters.name: Mrs. Ibidun Gloss
characters.significance: An astute education businesswoman who recognizes that Bepo is the intellectual bedrock of the school. She offers financial incentives and administrative support, personifying enlightened educational entrepreneurship in urban Lagos.

characters.name: Mrs. Grace Apeh
characters.significance: Bepo’s dependable second-in-command who steps up to manage crises during his emotional breakdown. She represents steady administrative continuity and the dependable cadre of female educational leaders in Nigeria.

characters.name: Mrs. Beke Egbin
characters.significance: The empathetic voice of mental wellness in the staff room. She advocates for treating teachers’ psychological vulnerabilities and stresses that leaders also need therapeutic care.

characters.name: Mr. Wande
characters.significance: A charismatic, deeply spiritual educator who interprets institutional stress through theological and moral lenses. He provides spiritual encouragement to Bepo while sparking lively staff room debates on faith vs. economic reality.

characters.name: Mr. Alabi & Mr. Fafore
characters.significance: Pragmatic classroom teachers who vocalize the harsh economic realities of Lagos—inflation, fuel hikes, and high rents—grounding the novel in contemporary Nigerian socio-economic difficulties.

characters.name: Angel
characters.significance: Represents the student body. Her heartfelt testimonial during the Inter-House sports and her leadership during the peaceful student protest directly influence Bepo’s historic decision at the airport.

characters.name: Bepo’s Spouse & UK Relatives
characters.significance: The catalysts of Bepo’s crisis. Living abroad in the UK, they view remaining in Nigeria as foolishness and relentlessly urge him to abandon Stardom Schools for Western opportunities.
